questions.prompt: Why does a HKCU CLSID entry override a machine-wide COM registration?
options: HKLM is only read during boot
HKCU takes precedence over HKLM for COM lookups, so a user-writable entry shadows the machine-wide one without needing admin rights
HKCU entries are digitally signed and therefore trusted first
COM objects are never registered in HKLM
questions.explanation: Because per-user class registrations take precedence, an attacker with no elevation can shadow a machine-wide CLSID and have their DLL loaded by any process that user runs.

questions.prompt: Why is process-creation logging (4688 or Sysmon Event ID 1) effectively blind to this technique class?
options: Those events are disabled by default on all systems
No anomalous process starts -- the malicious code loads into a legitimate, signed process, so detection requires image load events like Sysmon Event ID 7
The events are overwritten too quickly
COM hijacking terminates the logging service first
questions.explanation: The process itself is genuine and started for normal reasons. Only module-load telemetry reveals that an unexpected DLL entered it.

questions.prompt: What makes an abandoned CLSID an attractive hijacking target?
options: Abandoned CLSIDs run with SYSTEM privileges automatically
Software or a scheduled task still requests the GUID but nothing is registered for it, so hijacking produces no functional change anyone would notice
They are exempt from signature verification
They cannot be enumerated by forensic tools
questions.explanation: Because nothing was successfully loading before, the hijack introduces no visible breakage or behavior change to alert a user or administrator.

questions.prompt: What distinguishes DLL side-loading from search order hijacking?
options: Side-loading drops a legitimately signed vendor executable alongside a malicious DLL it loads, so the binary passes signature checks while the DLL beside it does not
They are the same technique with different names
questions.explanation: The executable is genuinely the vendor's and signed correctly. The abuse is in what sits next to it in a writable directory.
